applies_why: The judge text resolves a chain collision over Acts 2:30 by treating the absence of an explicit naming verse as decisive.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse'. Readings weighed: the judge may rest an underdetermined finding on the absence of a verse naming the channel, or it must instead assess the competing chains' footing and not decide by explicit naming.
why: Because the judge finds the point open solely because no verse names whose body is the channel, it applies the retired stating-verse test instead of weighing the chains by footing.
